summary: Dynamo-backed ingest coordinator heartbeats counted against tenant quota causing intermittent 429s during sustained backfills
description:
Issue summary:
Customer DataFlux AI reports intermittent 429 responses when running sustained backfill jobs that spawn many short-lived ingest workers. The jobs use our ingest coordinator which persists worker heartbeats to a Dynamo table. Around 2026-03-12 09:10 UTC they observed recurring 429 spikes lasting ~5–15 minutes and coinciding with coordinator scaling events.

Impact:
- Customer backfills fail with 429s and partial failures of ingestion pipelines.
- Observed increase in support ticket volume from their SRE and one production job failed a daily SLA.

Environment:
- Dedicated tenant on prod (us-east-1) with reserved capacity.
- Ingest coordinator is the Redwood-managed Dynamo-backed coordinator (version 2.7.1).
- Rate limiter and quota accounting services: rate-limiter-v3 behind edge-proxy cluster.

Steps to reproduce (reported by customer):
1) Start a backfill that spawns ~600 short-lived workers (lifecycle ~30–90s) coordinated by the ingest service.
2) Each worker writes a heartbeat to the Dynamo coordinator on start and periodically while active.
3) Backfill runs for 30–120 minutes.
4) Observe intermittent 429s on subsequent generation/embedding requests from the same tenant.

Observed behavior:
- Heartbeat write patterns correlate with spike in token/quota consumption for the tenant in our billing metrics (console shows spike in "request_count" aligned to heartbeat cadence).
- Customer sees 429s with response body: {"error": "rate_limited", "reason": "tenant_quota_exhausted"}.
- Rate-limit headers show X-RateLimit-Remaining dropping unexpectedly at the same time as heartbeats.

Expected behavior:
- Coordinator heartbeats should not count against tenant request/token quota. Only user-initiated API calls (generation/embeddings/chat) should be charged against quota. Heartbeats should be tagged as internal/health probes and excluded from tenant accounting.

Relevant logs & traces (anonymized):
- edge-proxy logs (2026-03-12T09:12:03Z): "POST /coord/heartbeat 200 tenant=DFX-001 trace=abc123 latency=23ms"
- rate-limiter trace (2026-03-12T09:12:03Z): "accounting: increment_request_count tenant=DFX-001 amount=1 source=proxied"
- ingest-coordinator (2026-03-12T09:11:58Z): "heartbeat write succeeded key=worker-123 ttl=90s"

Initial hypothesis:
- The ingest coordinator's heartbeat path was recently routed through the same public ingress as customer traffic and lacks the internal-probe header/marker. The rate-limiter treats the request as a normal tenant request and increments quota counters. A recent edge-proxy routing change (edge release 2026-03-11) added a proxy rewrite that removed the x-internal-probe header on requests originating from our managed coordinator tasks.

Requested outcome from customer:
- Immediate mitigation to prevent heartbeats consuming tenant quota (workaround) and a permanent fix so heartbeats are excluded from billing/accounting.
comments: 2026-03-12 10:00 - Support (Aisha Patel): Thanks for the report — we've opened this ticket and escalated to SRE. Can you share the backfill job id and a timestamp window for a 429 spike?
2026-03-12 10:12 - Customer (J. Morales, DataFlux AI): Backfill job id bf-20260312-09, spikes between 09:10–09:25 UTC. Attached: partial logs and worker count histogram.
2026-03-12 11:05 - SRE (Ravi Kapoor): Noted correlation with edge release on 2026-03-11. Pulling ingress rewrite and rate-limiter traces. Assigning to rate-limiter and proxy owners.
2026-03-12 13:30 - Proxy Eng (S. Liu): We verified a config entry in edge-release-2026-03-11 that normalizes headers for coordinator traffic; will test preserving x-internal-probe.
2026-03-13 09:15 - Billing (M. Novak): We are holding any invoice adjustments pending confirmation of misattribution; will create a billing reconciliation snapshot for affected window.
2026-03-14 08:40 - SRE (Ravi Kapoor): Temporary mitigation pushed: edge-proxy rule updated to preserve x-internal-probe for coordination service CIDR. Monitoring for reduced quota increments.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 - Trace analysis: Joined edge-proxy traces with rate-limiter logs — heartbeats are proxied as POST /coord/heartbeat and do not contain internal marker header. rate-limiter treats them as tenant requests and increments counters with tenant id tag.
2026-03-12 - Infra config: edge-release-2026-03-11 included a header normalization rule that removed non-whitelisted headers; the ingest coordinator's internal-probe header was not whitelisted.

2026-03-12 - Repro: Replayed a synthetic backfill in staging with 800 short-lived workers and observed quota counter increase when proxy removed internal header. With header preserved, quotas are unchanged.

2026-03-13 - Mitigation plan: 1) Patch edge-proxy whitelist to keep x-internal-probe for coordinator CIDR; 2) Add server-side defensive check in rate-limiter to ignore /coord/heartbeat endpoints regardless of headers; 3) Create billing reconciliation for 2026-03-12 09:00–09:30 UTC for DataFlux AI.
2026-03-14 - Next steps: Prepare release notes for proxy fix, schedule small changelist to rate-limiter (ignore path based) and test on canary dedicated tenant.
